world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Elizabeth Hall. 2018. A phonological analysis of Riang Lang. In Hiram Ring & Felix Rau (eds), Papers from the Seventh International Conference on Austroasiatic Linguistics (JSEALS Special Publication 3), 77-86. Honolulu: University of Hawai'i Press.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Modern phonology of the sister language Riang Lang [ril] (rian1261); the closest first-hand account of syllable prominence and tone in the Riang subgroup; open access on eVols but downloads were refused (not reachable by automated download) by automated download. Not the same Glottolog language as yinc1238.

sources.citation: Peter Lang publisher page for Thway 2010 (document 1136060).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Softcover only (US$82.95), no e-book or preview; summary mentions phonetics, phonology and tonology, not stress.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid pages yinc1238 and rian1261 with reference lists (Hammarström et al.).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: yinc1238 has only Thway 2008 and Thway 2010 as descriptive references; rian1261 lists Hall 2018 (phonology, 10 pp.), Shorto 2013, Shintani 2014 (dictionary), Sidwell 2015, Luce 1985, Scott & Hardiman 1900, Yan & Zhou 1995/2012 (all comparative/wordlist).

Secondary. Treats Riang Lang (ril) and Riang Lai/Yinchia (yin) as varieties of one language; gives Hall 2018's consonant and vowel charts for Riang Lang and says it 'is sesquisyllabic and has two tones', word template ((C)ə̆(C)).(C)(C)V(C). No stress statement.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2018. Change Request 2018-001 (yin: reference name Yinchia -> Riang Lai) and 2018-002 (ril -> Riang Lang), adopted 2019-01-25.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Identity only: 'In Myanmar this group referes to themselves as Riang Lai'; CR 2018-002 notes 'there is also a Riang Lai group [yin]'. Nothing on phonology.

sources.citation: H. L. Shorto. 2013 [1964]. Riang-Lang Vocabulary: compiled from the materials collected by G. H. Luce. Asia-Pacific Linguistics 5 / SEAMLES 4. Canberra: ANU. 195 pp. hdl:1885/9781.

sources.note: The only published description of Yinchia; Part B (ch. 8 syllable structure), Part C (tones, ch. 9-10) and ch. 12 (phonological word) are where any statement on stress/prominence in sesquisyllables would sit; would settle whether the language is described as tonal without word stress.
